sources.entry: TimeMachineEjector - Menu bar app that ejects your Time Machine backup disk when a backup finishes and mounts it again when a scheduled backup is due. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/wata/TimeMachineEjector) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: A macOS menu bar app that ejects a Time Machine backup disk after each backup finishes and remounts it when the next scheduled backup is due.
summary.what_it_does: Watches Time Machine and unmounts the backup disk once a backup and its cleanup are finished, so the disk can be unplugged at any time. When a scheduled backup is due, it mounts the disk again, following the frequency set in Time Machine settings, and does nothing if automatic backups are off. The menu bar icon shows a Time Machine badge while a backup runs, and the menu reports whether the disk is connected, ejected, or backing up, with progress and the time of the latest backup. Users can start a backup manually with Back Up Now, disable the behavior to keep the disk mounted, and enable Launch at Login. The app is distributed as a signed and notarized build with automatic updates, and can be installed from Releases or via Homebrew.
use_cases: Unplug an external Time Machine drive without ejecting it manually in Finder
Keep a backup disk disconnected between backups
Start an immediate Time Machine backup from the menu bar
Check whether a backup is still running before unplugging the drive
Let scheduled Time Machine backups keep working with an ejected disk
how_to_run: Or download the latest pre-built application from the Releases page and move it to /Applications
Open the app once and turn on Launch at Login from the menu bar icon
Development: ./scripts/install.sh builds a Release build and replaces /Applications/TimeMachineEjector.app (use --no-launch to skip launching)
Development: ./scripts/release.sh [--notes] bumps the version, builds a zip, updates appcast.xml, and publishes a GitHub Release (--no-publish stops before committing)
notable: Waits until Time Machine reports the backup is no longer running before ejecting, so post-copy cleanup is not interrupted
Mounts the ejected disk when a scheduled backup is due, following Time Machine's own schedule
Menu bar icon shows a Time Machine badge during a backup as a cue not to unplug
Unmounts other volumes on the same disk too, like ejecting in Finder; the disk is unmounted, not powered off
Signed and notarized, with automatic updates
caveats: Only the disk's volumes are unmounted; the disk is not powered off
Does nothing when automatic Time Machine backups are turned off
